0.desc: Continuous cellular sheets of closely packed cells with large, pale-to-mid purple nuclear profiles and a streaming or fascicular texture; little blank background. Exemplars are internally consistent and drawn from Slides A-D only.

1.desc: Densely cellular sheets with somewhat smaller, more tightly packed and more uniformly stained nuclear profiles than C0, minimal blank space, and occasional small vessel profiles; exemplars are drawn from Slides A-D only.

2.desc: Tissue-rich cellular fields with variable nuclear density and local blank gaps or tissue interfaces; a minority of low-margin exemplars sit against fibrous strands. Represented across all eight slides.

3.desc: Near-empty white background with isolated dark specks or debris-like fragments and occasional detached edge material; tissue content is inconsistent and often minimal.

4.desc: Predominantly blank fields crossed by thin fibrous tissue strands, narrow section-boundary fragments with scattered spindle-shaped nuclei, and occasional small vessels; a minority of low-margin exemplars are clearly more cellular, as expected at interfaces.

5.desc: Pale pink amorphous, granular material with faint cell-outline remnants and comparatively few intact nuclear profiles; several exemplars contain dense clusters of dark fragmented nuclear debris and one shows a strongly haematoxylin-dense deposit. Present on seven of the eight slides and forming large coherent territories on individual slides.

6.desc: Cellular tissue abutting blank space or section boundaries, with cohesive nuclear-rich groups on one side and open background on the other; nuclear content remains high within the tissue portion. Represented across all eight slides.

centralQuestion.question: Do neoplastic cells in control and PLX-treated tumours have different morphologies?
centralQuestion.roleOfThisStage: Establish whether neoplastic-cell morphology differs between frozen tissue contexts, before interpreting within-context treatment comparisons.
centralQuestion.plainLanguageAnswer: The image-defined tissue contexts have distinguishable but overlapping nuclear profiles. Whether those differences generalise across held-out mice is quantified by the tile-level classifiers.

analysisContract.clustering: frozen; no refitting or outcome-driven K selection
analysisContract.primaryMorphologyGate: matched, non-edge CellViT neoplastic nuclei with type probability >=0.70 and geometry QC
analysisContract.primaryHierarchy: nucleus -> tile median -> equal tiles within mouse -> equal mice
analysisContract.allNucleiPooledView: descriptive only; never used for treatment inference
analysisContract.classifierValidation: leave one mouse/WSI out; preprocessing fit on training mice only
analysisContract.clusterIdentityScope: run-local; C# values are not aligned across cohorts

morphology_plus_composition.reason: One or more leave-one-mouse-out test folds lack the complete run-local class set.

fully_supported_cellular.supportNote: Each included cluster passes 20 tiles and 500 high-confidence neoplastic nuclei in every one of 8 mice.

morphology_only.reason: At least two strict-cellular clusters are required for classification.

morphology_plus_composition.reason: At least two strict-cellular clusters are required for classification.

interpretationRules: Good morphology-only performance across held-out mice supports cross-slide concordance between nuclear shape and tissue context.
A material gain after adding composition suggests clusters are distinguished partly by cellular mixture or density.
Poor held-out-mouse performance despite within-section separation is compatible with slide, stain, or segmentation specificity.
Classification accuracy is not independent pathology validation and makes no treatment-effect claim.

limitations: Only 8 mice are available, with one WSI per mouse.
Clusters outside the provenance-resolved morphology-evaluable role gate have neoplastic morphology shown as N/A, not zero.
Cluster labels and nuclear measurements originate from the same H&E sections; classification is internal concordance, not independent validation.
No anatomical identity, lymph-node identity, necrosis, or drug-affected label is assigned without pathologist review.
The all-nuclei pooled view overweights large slides and nucleus-rich tiles and is descriptive only.
Area and perimeter, and several outline features, are correlated; they are complementary views rather than independent confirmations.
